sources.title: Discover Liberia: entry and visas
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Liberia National Tourism Authority .gov.lr visitor portal publishes current national entry and visa guidance.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Citizens of ECOWAS member states may enter without a visa.

sources.title: ECOWAS current Member States
sources.publisher: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current ECOWAS Commission member-state page lists the 12 current members, including Liberia, needed to map the ordinary passport cohort.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Benin, Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea Bissau, Liberia, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, The Gambia, Togo.

sources.title: ECOWAS press statement on AES withdrawal
sources.jurisdiction: Economic Community of West African States
sources.officialityEvidence: The current ECOWAS Commission statement directs relevant authorities inside and outside member States to maintain the specified treatment for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens pending agreed modalities.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Permettre aux citoyens des pays concernés de continuer à jouir ... du droit de circulation ... sans visa.

sources.title: Liberia Visa on Arrival application portal
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Liberia Immigration Service portal sets the actual online-preapproved Visa on Arrival workflow, airport limit and embassy-in-residence-country restriction.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If there is a Liberian embassy in your country, you are required to apply for your visa directly at the embassy.

policies.title: ECOWAS and continuing AES ordinary passports: visa-free entry to Liberia
policies.summary: Liberia’s National Tourism Authority says ECOWAS citizens may enter without a visa. The ECOWAS withdrawal arrangement continues visa-free movement for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger citizens, extending the supported foreign cohort to all 14 former/continuing ECOWAS issuers.
conditions: Applies only to the named foreign ordinary passports for the normal short-visitor baseline.
The AES-transition treatment for Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger is expressly pending full future-relation modalities; ECOWAS calls it effective until further notice.
Passport validity (the tourism authority advises six months and a blank page), border inspection, health requirements, security controls and individual admissibility remain applicable.
This policy does not establish residence, work, business-specific, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, refugee, laissez-passer, special-document or citizenship treatment.
